prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B060 with Buchwald and Hartwig. Ligand design (bulky, electron-rich phosphines and carbenes) made aryl amination general, predictable and scalable, and Hartwig's and Buchwald's mechanistic work on oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination explains why. Adoption is checkable in the literature and in process chemistry, and three decades of independent confirmation make it as mature as anything on the list. The attribution is the cleanest on the table: two independent, equal contributors and no omitted decisive person. The 2010 prize honoured C-C coupling; a citation that names carbon-nitrogen bond formation explicitly, as Zou asks, answers the continuation objection in the text itself. After the first-round exchange I accept that B026 is the broader and more novel idea, but I do not think its support count settles the question of what was new chemically.
statement.case_against: The case against B060 is the one I stated before and I have not found a rebuttal to all of it. It can be read as a successor to the 2010 prize, Sparr's point that a methods prize has lower conceptual novelty is a fair description of how some colleagues will see it, and only two members prefer it. Kosugi's tin-amide precedent keeps the priority history from being perfectly tidy, although I still judge it a precursor and not the decisive step. If five members hold B026 as their first choice with a shared trio, a final vote may well go that way, and I should not insist that my field preference outweighs that scientific judgment.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, argues that B026 has a testable, quantitative mechanism (ternary-complex cooperativity, degradation kinetics), that cereblon unifies glues and PROTACs, and that the absence of an approved PROTAC is the strongest objection but not disqualifying.
responses.response: The ternary-complex kinetics are a real quantitative basis and I do not dispute them. My standard for maturity is adoption seen in independent work, and approved cereblon-dependent glues plus hundreds of laboratories meet that for the principle, so I no longer treat the missing approved PROTAC as disqualifying by itself. Where we still differ is on what is new chemically. The PROTAC arm is linker and ligand design on known E3 ligase ligands, and you yourself note that the cereblon story is partly pharmacology. I would support B026 only with a citation worded around induced proximity as a designable chemical principle, not around drugs, and I would rather the committee state openly that the glue and PROTAC arms are two lines.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B026 first because it is completely new and already has consequences, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa covering both the heterobifunctional and monovalent branches, and he is open to Ciulli replacing Deshaies.
responses.response: I agree that novelty plus consequence is the right test and B026 passes it. On attribution I would resist replacing Deshaies with Ciulli only if the reports confirm Deshaies's early conceptual role, since Ciulli's VHL ligands made the design rational but came after the concept. Any three-person cut leaves out Sakamoto, Kim, Gray, Ciulli or Ito, and the committee should accept that cost knowingly. If the committee goes with B026, I consider Handa's cereblon work the most defensible third name, because it is the only one that explains an old drug mechanism in chemical terms. My own preference remains B060 because its attribution needs no such compromise.

responses.point: Zou now supports Buchwald and Hartwig without Kosugi and asks that the citation say carbon-nitrogen coupling explicitly, using Hartwig's mechanistic evidence to rebut the 2010 overlap.
responses.response: I accept both conditions and have kept the citation wording explicit. I would add Buchwald's contribution to the same argument: the ligand-generation work (biaryl phosphines) is what made the method general with free amines and aryl chlorides, and so it is not an incremental extension of the C-C catalysts. That pairing of mechanism from Hartwig and ligand design from Buchwald is the strongest answer to the continuation worry. I note that only the two of us hold this position, so we should be honest that it is a minority view going into the vote.

responses.point: Sparr says Buchwald and Hartwig have the cleanest attribution but a methods prize carries lower conceptual novelty than a new principle, and she would not oppose it as a synthetic-chemistry anchor.
responses.response: I take the point, and I respect that you will not oppose. I would argue that novelty should be judged by what the method changed, not by how abstract the principle sounds: a reaction that made a previously unreliable bond routine altered the logic of retrosynthesis and drug manufacture. I do not claim this beats a new modality. On your own first choice, B031, I share the reservations raised by others (in vivo evidence, the omission of Pappu and Mittag), which is why I do not rank it above B060, though I agree that the physical-chemical content is real.

responses.point: Chabes accepts the C-N coupling case on merit, defends base editing as a defined chemical conversion, and keeps B026 first with a single citation covering PROTACs and glues.
responses.response: Thank you. On base editing, I accept that engineered deaminase chemistry at a programmed site is a defined conversion, but the chemical invention is the protein engineering, and it comes shortly after the 2020 prize, so I keep it low. On your single-citation point for B026, I would not object to one citation if it names the shared principle precisely, but it should not imply that the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism were one discovery by one group.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats C-N coupling as a distinct achievement or as covered by the 2010 prize; I judge it distinct but cannot prove how colleagues will read it.
Whether Kosugi's tin-amide work deserves more than a historical mention; I rely on recall and have not verified its scope.
Whether the glue and PROTAC lines are one achievement or two, and whether any three-person cut for B026 can be defended given Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito.
Current clinical status of PROTACs; nobody in this process has verified it, and my statements on maturity depend on that.
If B026 clearly leads at the final vote, I will have to decide whether a minority preference for B060 should hold or yield; I have not decided that.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no known personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or to any credited name in B026, B067, B031 or the other shortlisted parts. My mentor Masamune and my institutions (Chalmers, KTH, Lund, Tartu) are not linked to them in my profile. I note that I am a synthetic organic chemist and may favour methodology, and that Linke and Sparr are Lund colleagues, an institutional tie only.
